title: Launch Risk & Exception Endorsement Form
content:
Purpose:
This working form captures the minimum security evidence and reviewer endorsements required to approve a product release that has either a planned deviation from baseline security controls or requires a formal exception to RBAC/telemetry/export rules. It is intended to be attached to the release ticket and persisted with launch artifacts.

Scope
- Applies to all releases that touch: RBAC v2 policies, audit-log schema changes, SIEM export formats, or the automated evidence collection pipeline.
- Not a replacement for full Threat Modeling; it’s a release-level gate to ensure observability and accountability are adequate when controls change.

Quick summary (one-line):
- Release name / tag: <INSERT_RELEASE_NAME>
- Release ticket: JIRA-<insert> (example: JIRA-SEC-4123)
- Owner (release lead): <NAME>
- Proposed production date: <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Risk tier: Low / Medium / High (pick one)

Checklist: Pre-launch verification (must be completed or have approved exception)
1) RBAC v2 policy changes
   - Describe change (short): <free text>
   - Confirmed effect surface area: <services, endpoints, admin consoles>
   - Tests executed:
     * Unit tests for role bindings (yes/no): <yes/no>
     * Integration test that simulates token exchange and scoped access (yes/no): <yes/no>
     * Backward compatibility check with legacy roles (yes/no): <yes/no or N/A>
   - Rollback plan for RBAC change documented (link): <confluence or PR>
   - Required approvers: sec-policies-owner, infra-ops, product-security. Date approvals obtained: <YYYY-MM-DD>

2) Audit log schema changes (v2/v3)
   - Schema version being deployed: <e.g., audit-schema-v3>
   - Schema diff summary: <added fields / removed fields / renamed fields>
   - Consumers impacted: (list) e.g., SIEM parser, forensic tools, billing pipeline
   - Backfill / migration approach: none / migration job / adapter shim (describe)
   - Validation tests run:
     * Schema conformance test suite (pass/fail): <pass/fail>
     * Sample log run-through against existing SIEM parser (pass/fail): <pass/fail>
   - Evidence artifact (attach/export id): <s3://... or confluence page>

3) SIEM export and parsing
   - SIEM destination(s): <e.g., Splunk: index=redwood-prod, Elastic: logs-prod>
   - Field mapping doc: <link or attach>
   - Message format (newline JSON / NDJSON / other): <format>
   - Enrichment rules applied (yes/no). If yes, list keys added: <user_id, trace_id, role_hint>
   - Test ingest snapshot provided (link): <link to sample index or test run>
   - Alerting change required? (yes/no). If yes, list alerts to be updated.

4) Evidence automation (release packaging for audit)
   - Evidence bundle includes:
     * RBAC diffs and approval timestamps
     * Audit-log schema artifacts and validation runs
     * SIEM ingest test results and mapping file
     * Automated smoke-run logs (token-level traces masked)
   - Evidence packaging method: automated CI artifact / manual upload (specify)
   - Retention/hand-off: where the bundle is stored and for how long (e.g., S3:/evidence/releases/<release>/, retention 365 days)

5) Exception approval (if any control is being relaxed)
   - Exception id (assign on approval): <EXC-YYYY-NNN>
   - Scope of exception (which control / resource / duration): <free text>
   - Justification summary (business need + mitigation): <free text>
   - Compensating controls in place: <e.g., increased monitoring, canary traffic limits, timeboxed window>
   - Maximum duration requested: <days>
   - Required approvers for exception: security-lead, CISO-delegate, legal if PII involved.
   - Exception escalation path (if risk materializes): Pager oncall, SEC-INC response, pause rollout procedure (link)

6) Launch-time validation steps (must be executed during rollout)
   - Verify audit logs emitted for 5 representative journeys (link to automated smoke job output)
   - Ensure SIEM parser is ingesting new schema fields without errors for 60 minutes after rollout begins
   - Confirm RBAC policy behaves correctly for at least these roles: admin, read-only-service-account, cross-region-replica
   - Binary rollback toggle tested and available in <deploy system>

Reviewer endorsement table (sign-off required; free-text comments encouraged)
- Security reviewer: <name> | role: <e.g., sec-engineer> | approves? (yes/no) | date: <YYYY-MM-DD> | comments: <string>
- Infra reviewer: <name> | role: <e.g., infra-eng> | approves? (yes/no) | date: <YYYY-MM-DD> | comments: <string>
- Product owner: <name> | role: <e.g., product-hosted-api> | approves? (yes/no) | date: <YYYY-MM-DD> | comments: <string>
- Compliance/legal: <name or N/A> | approves? (yes/no) | date: <YYYY-MM-DD> | comments: <string>

Decision guide (for reviewers):
- If any of the following are true, mark release as HOLD until remediated or an exception is approved:
  * Audit logs are missing or malformed for core auth flows
  * RBAC change removes oversight roles without compensating control
  * SIEM ingest fails or shows parsing errors for >=10% of sample events

- Low/Medium/High risk guidance (examples):
  * Low — cosmetic telemetry field renames, no consumer breakage, automated tests green
  * Medium — schema change that requires a short-lived adapter; mitigations include increased sampling and a rollback window
  * High — RBAC expansion or reduction for admin-level access, PII fields moving into logs, or cross-account export changes

Temporary launch exemption pattern (approved exceptions SHOULD follow this pattern):
- Short duration (max 14 days unless otherwise approved)
- Explicit compensating controls (e.g., 2x alert sensitivity, additional manual review for flagged events)
- Automated evidence collection turned on for the duration and stored in the evidence bucket
- A mandatory post-mortem and retrospective checklist to close the exception

Record keeping: required fields to store with the release artifact
- Release id, ticket link, exception id (if any), approver list + timestamps, evidence bundle link, schema version, SIEM test artifacts, automated run IDs.

Open questions / follow-ups (notes to self and reviewers):
- Do we need to version the SIEM parser config in git per release or keep a single rolling config? (Impact: rollback complexity)
- Should RBAC v2 changes require a separate canary namespace to be exercised before rollouts? (Action: propose infra runbook)
- Evidence bundle size and retention policy may conflict with compliance retention rules for certain regions (Legal to weigh in).

Action items (owners and rough ETA):
- Attach sample SIEM ingest run to this doc: Marcus Chen — due 2025-11-12
- Draft exception template (machine-readable) to allow automated approval tracking: Lina Gómez — due 2025-11-19
- Add a small post-launch smoke job that checks audit log fields within 5 minutes of new deployment: Ethan Brooks — due 2025-11-08

Notes / working draft markers:
- This is intentionally concise to be easy to sign-off in the release flow. More detailed templates (full RBAC diff export, migration scripts) should be attached as linked artifacts.
- Keep temporarily incomplete fields as TODOs in the release ticket rather than blocking if exception process is used and approvers accept compensating controls.

Revision log:
- 2025-11-05: initial draft (Aisha Patel)
- 2025-11-12: added SIEM test checklist and sample fields (Marcus Chen)
- 2026-03-10: clarified exception duration guidance and added required approvers for PII-related changes (Lina Gómez)

Sign-off (final block — to be copied into release ticket):
I have reviewed the attached evidence and the compensating controls described above. I endorse the release to proceed under the stated conditions or acknowledge the exception.

- Security reviewer name: ____________________  date: __________
- Infra reviewer name: ______________________  date: __________
- Product owner name: ______________________  date: __________
- Compliance/legal: _________________________  date: __________

(End of document)
